instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the lower third. Take the packaging and the plastic disk off the ham.
Set the ham cut side down in a shallow roasting pan. Cover the ham and the pan loosely with foil.

Bake for 12 to 16 minutes per pound, which is about 1 hour 15 minutes for a 5 lb ham. You're heating it to 135°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut a slice from the thickest part near the bone: it should be steaming hot all the way through.
While the ham bakes, stir the 1/2 cup honey, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp Dijon, 1/2 tsp garlic powder and 1/8 tsp cloves together in a small bowl.
When the ham is hot, take it out and turn the oven up to 425°F. Remove the foil. Brush the ham with the glaze in 2 to 3 generous coats, getting it between the slices.
Put the ham back in the oven uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes, until the glaze is browned and the ham reaches 140°F in the middle.
Let the ham rest for 15 minutes before you cut it.
Serve the slices with the pan juices spooned over.

Store the leftover ham in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. For the freezer, freeze sliced ham with a spoonful of pan juices for up to 2 months. Thaw it overnight in the fridge, then reheat it covered at 300°F with a splash of water.
method_notes: Spend With Pennies (4.99 from 89 ratings) leads: bake the fully cooked spiral ham covered at 325°F to 135°F, then brush on the honey glaze and finish at 425°F to 140°F. Its glaze has melted butter, which is left out here to keep the dish dairy-free; the honey, brown sugar, mustard and cloves still make a thick glaze. The amounts are halved for a 5 lb half ham, which still leaves leftovers for days. Check the ham's label for gluten-free, since some glazed or cured hams carry gluten. Jessica Gavin's version (5.0 from 5 ratings) uses pineapple juice and a longer bake and agrees on the covered bake and the 425°F finish.
